basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; cerebellar hypoplasia and seizures also affect the neurologic axis.
Glutaminase deficiency causes hyperglutaminemia with developmental delay and progressive cerebellar ataxia in 3/3 patients.
Viral infection umbrella; neurologic disease characterizes rabies but is not shared across the entire group.
Ischemic necrosis of a reproductive organ; vascular causation alone does not establish a cardiovascular disorder or endocrine dysfunction.
Defined by endocrine neoplasia involving thyroid C cells, adrenal medulla and parathyroids; other organ damage is not consistently common.
Glomerular immunoglobulin deposition causes proteinuria and progressive renal dysfunction; associated lymphoproliferative disorders are separate diseases.
Xq deletions commonly cause ovarian dysgenesis or insufficiency; neurologic, muscular and renal manifestations depend on deletion extent.
Viral infection umbrella with differing respiratory, salivary and neurologic targets; no additional organ is consistently affected across the group.
A benign capillary vascular tumor arising in the eyelid; unrelated nervous-system ancestry does not establish neurologic involvement.
A gastric or duodenal ulcer perforates the gastrointestinal wall; secondary infection is not inherent to every perforation.
Inherited corneal endothelial degeneration; corneal guttata occur in 12/12 patients.
Inherited lens opacity causing reduced visual acuity; no extraocular disease is established.
Isolated failure of spermatogenesis causes infertility and azoospermia; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ damage is established.
Benign glandular proliferation confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Malignant squamous epithelial tumor originating in the colon or rectum.
Persistent dermal histiocytic proliferation produces widespread papules; blood abnormalities are occasional and leukemia is a rare separate disease.
Pigment obstructs trabecular outflow, causing elevated intraocular pressure and glaucomatous optic nerve damage within the ocular axis.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the classic late-infantile course.
Carcinoma originates in maxillary sinus respiratory mucosa; oral-cavity and bone ancestry does not override the defined site of origin.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining features; intellectual disability occurs in 26/33. Renal disease is less common in BBS1 and omitted under the cap.
Congenital structural defect of the inferior eyelid; associated syndromes or facial clefts are not universal.
Cobalamin-processing defect; developmental delay and anemia/neutropenia in 2/2; structural heart defects and pulmonary arterial hypertension in 1/2. Very small cohort.
Gastroschisis-type abdominal wall malformation with exteriorized bowel; the defining lesion involves the abdominal wall and gastrointestinal tract.
Psychiatric substance-related umbrella; encephalopathy and other organ-specific alcohol diseases are distinct subtypes, not universal damage across the group.
Congenital absence of selected teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
